title: More than half of Arkansas is in exceptional drought
lede: Exceptional drought (D4) is the worst of the Drought Monitor's five drought levels.
We show how much of each state's land was at that level on four maps.

big.label: of Arkansas's land area in exceptional drought (D4), map valid Nov 17, 2026

chart.title: Share of each state's land in drought, four Drought Monitor maps
series: Extreme drought or worse (D3 or D4)

facts.text: 55.8% of Arkansas was in exceptional drought (D4) on the Nov 17 map, up from 49.5% a week earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026

facts.text: It was 19.4% four weeks earlier (Oct 20) and 0% a year earlier (Nov 18, 2025).
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026

facts.text: 86.5% of Arkansas was in extreme drought or worse (D3 or D4), up from 84.6% a week earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026

facts.text: 60 of Arkansas's 75 counties had some exceptional drought, up from 57 a week earlier and 32 four weeks earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026

facts.text: In 41 of those counties, at least half the land was in exceptional drought.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026

facts.text: Louisiana: 22.3% in exceptional drought, 59.9% in D3 or worse. Mississippi: 27.8% in exceptional drought, 53.6% in D3 or worse.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 17, 2026
